chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Dharih, who said:

I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) in the Sanctuary (Haram) before entering it or after entering it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It does not harm you whichever of those you do; and if you bathe in Mecca, there is no problem, and if you bathe in your house when you settle in Mecca, there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (Haram), specifically referring to the sacred precincts of Mecca
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: When and where can one perform the ritual bath (ghusl) before entering the Haram of Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (rukhsah) regarding the timing and location of ghusl for pilgrims, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease in ritual purity. It underscores that the sanctity of the Haram is not contingent upon the specific site of ablution, allowing believers to perform ghusl either within the sacred precincts or in their accommodations upon arrival. This ruling alleviates potential logistical burdens for pilgrims, ensuring that the spiritual state of Ihram is accessible regardless of immediate physical circumstances.
